text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- About 60 percent of Poles do not understand the planned social security reform, a survey by the PBS polling agency shows.

- The Polish transport ministry's tender committee has recommended that a consortium of domestic firms, Autostrada Wielkopolska, be granted a licence to build the A-2 toll motorway linking the German border and the central city of Lodz.
- Chemical plant Rokita has to postpone the planned share issue until it sorts out environmental problems, the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) said.
- Only four brokerage houses have so far applied to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) for permits to trade foreign stocks, KPW said.
- Poland's construction industry completed 54,900 flats in 1996, the worst result in the last forty years, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's corporate sector lost 603,200 working hours in 1996 through strikes of over 44,000 employees, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Scania truck maker has opened a 1,220 square metres spare parts warehouse the in the central city of Kutno, Scania said.

- Szczecin shipyard has launched the hull of Helen Schulte universal container ship to be completed in March this year. The vessel will be adapted to carry 1,654 containers. The shipyard is planing to launch 22 ships this year.

- The Wielkopolskie Fabryki Mebli furniture makers' sales in 1996 were 90 million zlotys, the company said. Around 60 percent of its products were sold on western markets, 30 percent in Poland and 10 percent in the CIS countries.
NOWA EUROPA

- Fleming Capital Markets, Lazard Brothers, Nomura, Salomon Brothers and Belgium's MCBBL will guarantee the $50 million convertible bond issue of the Stalexport steel producer and trader to be traded on the London Stock Exchange, Stalexport's board member Jacek Czeladko said.
- USAID will grant $6.5 million to support development of Poland's small and medium size businesses, USAID said.

- The city authorities of Bialystok, northeastern Poland, have received offers from 12 foreign firms planning to invest in the region, which is expected to become the eastern border area of the European Union in a few years time.

- The Gdansk refinery (RG) employees are planning to go on strike demanding refinery's shares, indexation of last year's salaries' and restructuring of the plant, the company's Solidarity trade union leader Andrzej Cenacewicz said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's employers presented 878,900 job offers to employment offices last year, compared with 914,200 offers in 1995, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's insurance firms are offering preferential rates for driver liability policies to car importers.
